identity.title: Genomic resequencing of low nicotine tobacco germplasm identifies novel allelic variations contributing to reduced alkaloid accumulation in tobacco.

content.abstract: In response to proposed regulations on non-addictive nicotine levels in tobacco products, researchers are screening tobacco germplasm for natural alleles associated with reduced alkaloid accumulation. Here, we re-evaluated total alkaloid contents in 15 low-nicotine accessions and identified associated allelic variations through whole-genome resequencing. Two novel nic1 alleles, nic1-5 and nic1-6, were identified and associated with suppressed nicotine biosynthetic gene expression and reduced alkaloid accumulation. Furthermore, we also identified a single-nucleotide deletion in NtMYC2a and a C-to-A substitution in NtNUP2, both causing frameshifts and resulting in premature termination codons. The NtMYC2a mutant was associated with dramatically reduced alkaloid levels in low-nicotine accessions, whereas CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of NtNUP2 did not significantly reduce nicotine content in the edited lines. These findings expand our known nic1 allelic diversity and facilitate allele pyramiding as a strategy for breeding ultra-low-nicotine tobacco cultivars.
